short_answer: Wayne Allyn Root is a real, long known handicapper. Filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission show he was chief executive of Winning Edge International, a public company that sold handicapping advice until it sold its operating assets in 2007. Today VegasWinners.com sells his picks for $30 each and lists a phone number for customer service.

Whether his picks make money is not something we could check. The site shows short streaks and old season highlights, such as "2019 NBA Playoffs 28-13 (68%)", chosen by the seller, with no log of every pick, line and post time. Its terms say there are no guaranteed winners, and its refund policy offers no refunds.
Treat Root as a famous seller with marketing records, not a proven winner. If you buy, buy one pick at a time, record it with the line you could get, and judge it after a few hundred picks.

guarantee: VegasWinners.com does not sell a guarantee. The full refund policy reads: "No refunds, but credit applied in specific individual cases." It does not say which cases. The terms of service add that "there are no guaranteed winners" and that the site does not guarantee a winner from any picks sold.

That is a change in tone from his earlier business. A Columbia Magazine profile from Fall 2008 said Root sold his picks as "Guaranteed Winners!" for as much as $25,000 for a season package. We found no such guarantee language on the current site.

claims_note: Every record on the site is a short window or a selected category, such as "Pinnacle" or "Gold Standard" plays, picked by the seller. A 7-1 or 5-0 run says very little, because any active handicapper has hot stretches somewhere. The profile's season highlights stop in early 2020.

The numbers are hard to square with Root's own words. In a 2004 Las Vegas Sun interview he said "the best gamblers in the world win 55 percent of their games overall" and that hitting 70 or 80 percent cannot be done. His current pages lead with 68% to 75% runs.

The dates do not hold one number either. The profile says active since 1985, which is 41 years, while the homepage says 37 years of winners. In a 2004 Daily Racing Form article, Root called himself "an entertainer and a salesman" and said everyone in sales puts their best foot forward.

The footer licensing line matches a 2021 press release that said VegasWinners was a registered sports gambling affiliate in West Virginia, Indiana, Colorado, New Jersey and Tennessee. Affiliate registration lets a company earn commissions from sportsbooks. It is not a check of anyone's picks.
record: What is independently verifiable: very little about results. Root's past business is on public record. A 10-KSB annual report filed with the SEC for the year ended 31 Jul 2007 shows Winning Edge International, with Root as chairman and chief executive, sold sports handicapping advice through a subsidiary, reported revenue of $5,863,137 and a net loss of $1,198,504 that year, and sold all of its operating assets to Betbrokers PLC in September 2007. Those filings describe the business, not whether the picks won.

What is the seller's own marketing: every win and loss figure on VegasWinners.com, from the homepage streaks to the 2017 to 2020 highlights on his profile. We found no full, searchable archive of his past picks with the line and post time, and no current season record. The picks for sale page still listed other handicappers' $30 picks dated December 2023 and February 2024.

Ownership has changed. An offering statement that Winners, Inc., the parent of VegasWinners, filed with the SEC in April 2026 says Root became its chief executive in July 2023, but that B. Michael Friedman has been chief executive since 30 Sep 2025, after it bought a prediction market business. The same filing reports unaudited revenue of $7,850 for 2025 and none for 2024. The VegasWinners About Us page still calls Root CEO of VegasWINNERS. We found no court or regulator action involving Root's handicapping business in our searches.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Wayne Allyn Root is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Root's pages lead with 68% to 75% runs. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found no review site entries from people who bought Root's picks. The closest thing to buyer experience is a 2023 TheRX thread where members who said they held yearly subscriptions argued about what he sent. The rest is forum opinion from 2005 and 2009, mostly about his TV show. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: Trustpilot had no page for vegaswinners.com, a Better Business Bureau search for VegasWinners returned no business, and we found no app store listing, no Reddit thread and no Covers forum thread from a buyer of Root's picks.

On TheRX forum, two members who each said they had a year long subscription to Root argued over the previous day's picks. One said Root's site showed only one play; the other said Root also emails subscribers a bonus play and more plays, and that he is "not greatest at updating" his site. If so, what the site shows may not match what subscribers receive.
In the same thread another member said he did not know who bets Root's picks and that buyers would do better spending the "root money" on a different service. He gave no results.

On the Sportsbook Review forum, the member who opened a thread about the Winning Edge TV show called its handicappers salesmen and frauds, and a later post in the thread called Root a liar. No evidence about specific picks or customers was given.
In the same thread a member listed each handicapper's best bet of the week from the previous day's show and said all of them lost, including Root's Colorado State pick. That is one week of picks.

In a Sportsbook Review thread about TV handicapping shows, a member who strongly disliked Root posted what he said was a promotional email from Root, saying his business had gone "100% web" through WinningEDGE.com and VegasWINNERS.com. Another member claimed Winning Edge had gone bankrupt; SEC filings show the company sold its assets in 2007.
In the same thread a member said he tracked the free picks from these shows and they usually hit more than 50%, but that he had never called the hotline or bought picks.

conflicts: The VegasWinners homepage loads a banner from betmgmpartners.com, the BetMGM affiliate program. A 2021 press release from the parent company said VegasWinners "intends to drive traffic to gaming operators for commission." A pick seller that earns from sportsbooks gains when readers bet more, win or lose.

VegasWinners also sells picks from other handicappers, including Al McMordie, and the parent company is a publicly quoted stock. Its press releases, such as the 2021 "over 73%" release, promote both the picks and the company.
strengths: A named company, a customer service phone number and email, and a written delivery policy explaining where purchased picks appear.
Single picks cost $30, so a buyer can test one pick without a large package.
The terms state plainly that there are no guaranteed winners, which is more honest than a "guaranteed" pitch.
His past business is documented in public SEC filings.
concerns: No full public record. Every figure on the site is a streak or season highlight chosen by the seller, and the profile's highlights stop in 2020.
No refunds. Credit is offered only in unnamed "specific individual cases".
Subscription prices were not shown, and the subscription link did not load.
The site carries a sportsbook affiliate banner, and the parent company described itself as an affiliate earning commissions.
The parent company reported almost no revenue in 2024 and 2025 and changed chief executive in 2025, while the store still lists picks dated 2023 and 2024.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, well known handicapper with a documented business history, and VegasWinners.com sells his picks with a listed phone number and terms. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the site publishes no full record.
How much does Wayne Allyn Root cost?
On 7 Nov 2026 his single picks on VegasWinners.com were $30 each. Subscription prices were not shown, and the homepage asked readers to email for a month or season deal.
Does Wayne Allyn Root have a verified record?

No. The win rates on his pages, such as 28-12-2 over three weeks or 28-13 in the 2019 NBA playoffs, are the seller's own figures with no log of every pick behind them, and Watchdog has no graded record for him.
Is Wayne Allyn Root worth it?

For $30 you get one pick from a famous handicapper with a short write up. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of bets, and the site gives no refunds if they lose.
